intent: The popup of a submenu, portalled and positioned beside its DropdownMenuSubTrigger, that lists the submenu's items.
typical_uses: The second-level list of actions behind a DropdownMenuSubTrigger

dont_use_when.situation: The first-level popup opened by a DropdownMenuTrigger

invariants.text: The submenu popup is in the DOM only while its submenu is open or animating closed; the kit passes no `keepMounted` to the portal.

Without `container`, the submenu popup portals into the container its enclosing DropdownMenuContent or DropdownMenuSubContent resolved, so a theme passed to the first-level popup holds in the submenu; its own `container` wins when given.
dropdown-menu.module.css sizes the submenu popup to its own content with an 8rem floor, not to the width of its sub-trigger.
The submenu opens on the physical right of its sub-trigger unless `side` says otherwise; the default does not flip in a right-to-left layout.
The popup fades and scales on open and close; under `prefers-reduced-motion` dropdown-menu.module.css drops the transform transition and keeps the fade.

anti_patterns.dont: Chain submenus more than one level deep
anti_patterns.do_instead: Flatten the deeper level into a group or radio group inside this popup; each extra level is another popup to reach by hover or arrow keys

a11y.by: the primitive's Menu.Popup renders role="menu"; dropdown-menu.test.tsx asserts the submenu item's closest [role="menu"] ancestor carries the submenu popup class

children.states: children is the submenu popup's rows, the parts listed under accepts
children.because: `React.ReactNode` is a union of elements, strings, numbers, fragments and more, which the compiler cannot state as one JSON type.

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the popup portals into; null and undefined both mean no container of its own
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers. The kit resolves it as `container ?? <the enclosing content's container>`, so an explicit null falls through like an absent prop.

sideOffset.states: sideOffset is the gap in pixels between the anchor and the popup, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
sideOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

alignOffset.states: alignOffset is the shift in pixels along the alignment axis, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
alignOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

collisionBoundary.states: collisionBoundary is the area the popup is kept inside, `clipping-ancestors`, an element, a list of elements or a rectangle
collisionBoundary.because: `'clipping-ancestors' | Element | Element[] | Rect` mixes a string with live DOM elements, which no JSON Schema type covers.

collisionPadding.states: collisionPadding is the space in pixels kept from the collision boundary, one number or a per-side object
collisionPadding.because: `number | { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

finalFocus.states: finalFocus decides where focus goes when the popup closes - true for the default, false for nowhere, a ref, or a function of the interaction type
finalFocus.because: `boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType) => boolean | HTMLElement | null | void)` mixes a boolean with a ref object and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the popup's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the popup's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, side, align, nested, instant, transitionStatus). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through dropdown-menu.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.reason: Composed through DropdownMenuContent; only its `container` is exposed, as a prop of the submenu popup itself.
Composed through DropdownMenuContent; its placement and collision props are exposed on the submenu popup itself.

bad.title: A DropdownMenuContent used as the submenu popup
bad.why: DropdownMenuContent keeps the first-level placement and sizing, so the submenu opens below the sub-trigger, over the rows beneath it, at the sub-trigger's width; DropdownMenuSubContent opens beside the sub-trigger and sizes to its content.
